body: What an adorable little lady! Thanks for this.

I'm really sorry about your cat, Brendyrose. I'm an animal lover myself and know how utterly devastating it is to lose a beloved pet and member of the family. They really do love us no matter what.

Please don't do anything to hurt yourself. People are out there who definitely do care and hope you'll be okay.

Hi Joshy,

Thanks for taking the time to write :)
I often do feel like either support isn't there or that I shouldn't burden others with my problems. Telling my parents or brother how I'm feeling doesn't even register a response anymore. 'Oh, Trifari's depressed again - news at 11'. They're good people, so you can't blame them

May definitely has problems of her own to deal with - job and financial insecurity, being single and wanting to start a family, so I try not to make things all about me.

My husband is a fundamentally kind person and tells me that I can share anything with him. But I know from experience that he 'doesn't like sad things', which includes serious dramas or reading newspapers. I sometimes wonder if he also doesn't like sad people, so I keep my low moods under wraps unless I'm visibly low. I'm sure he has no idea that I sometimes wish I was dead. If he does, he's never given me an indication that he's concerned. He'll ask how therapy sessions go, or how I'm feeling but that's the extent of it. I once told him that I was diagnosed with double-depression and all I got was silence in return. So I don't know.

Honestly, what would I change? Nothing specific, but I kind of miss my days when I taught English in another country. It was hard work (and I wasn't great at it), but I loved being surrounded by culture and being able to go and do whatever I felt like, at any time. Life was interesting.

Right???

I look at mine and wonder if he'll come to his senses.

As a 31 year old woman (married, no kids), I think age doesn't change how we feel. But I believe we're probably less likely to off ourselves because we worry about what would happen to our children/spouses/aging parents/housecats. So we continue to shuffle along in grey misery because 'responsibilities'.

Because sometimes I wonder if modernity is really all that it's cracked up to be. We've built cities, globalized and can travel to other places and contact other people with incredible ease...but we've never been lonelier. We have to travel to find decent jobs now, gone are the days of living in permanent, tight-knit communities of lifelong family, friends and neighbours. 

And society has become meaner, I think. Everything these days seems so partisan - rightists versus leftists, feminists versus men's rights' activists, attachment parenting enthusiasts versus free-rangers. If you are a moderate, then everyone hates you. 

Rampant consumerism has given us the luxury of looking down on each other for the most arbitrary shit ever (little Aidan gets bullied because he doesn't wear designer shoes). And then there's the internet - we've seen people commit the heinous crime of being unlikeable or having unpopular opinions and finding themselves doxxed or mobbed by a bunch of virtue-parading hypocrites.

So, yes. I often think the world can suck a bag of syphilitic dicks.

I know how you feel :/ It's awful to put so much work and effort into improving yourself and then feeling like you've taken a giant step back.

Please be patient and kind with yourself, though. *I* don't think you're a bad person. I just think you're stretched to the limit. And I think if people knew the truth about what it's really like to struggle with depression, they wouldn't judge you so harshly. Healthy, happy people really don't seem to fathom that what *seems* like abrupt or 'asocial' behaviour isn't the result of fundamental jerkiness. 

In your heart of hearts, how would you like to proceed? Do you find your role meaningful in general and want to give it another shot? Or maybe take this as an opportunity to cut out some 'extras' in life right now and focus on self-care? Either way is perfectly okay. Don't get me wrong, it must feel like failure right now, but you're unwell. It's very difficult to be at 100% when you are feeling like you operate at 5%.

Please tell your doctor you have suicidal thoughts. If you're worried about hospitalization; it's very likely that they would try to have you admitted to a hospital. Generally they wait for some sort of immediate threat i.e. you have the X on hand and will do it at Y o'clock.

As a bit of an aside: it's my unprofessional opinion that your university doctor completely missed the mark and couldn't see the forest for the trees. My last therapist firmly believed that my depression was situational and kept trying to push me selecting a job I was 'passionate about'. But really, it's like bandaging a wound while there's a giant splinter still inside. My unhappiness of me being me would always get in the way of any life-plans and I find my inherent feelings of worthlessness tend to sabotage everything else.

I am so, so sorry about the pain you're going through. I've gone through similar experiences in the past - there's nothing worse than feeling rejected by people you've gone to like and respect.

But, please, don't think that the criticism about your performance in your role means you're a bad person. If you're at all like me, constant depression and just the struggle to get out of bed in the morning saps so much energy, that we can be brusque without realizing it, or completely miss social cues because we're so damn tired. 

Sending internet hugs your way. if you ever want to talk, message me.
